findings.reason: without naming the classification owner/memo, an implementer may add a parallel cache or reader in `serve.py` rather than extend the shared one.
findings.text: §3's speed half imposes a "GET /crew under one second on 40 live pointers" gate but names no mechanism, while the per-pointer cost it must reduce is owned by `classify_pointer` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:7789`) and its already-persisted memo (`_read_classification_memo`, `reckon/crew/recovery.py:7306`); the plan cites `_crew_rows` but not that owner.

findings.reason: implementing §4 literally would either duplicate the SPA's rendering in Python or add a headless-browser test, whereas the fact belongs at the `/_discover` owner the pin reaches.
findings.text: §4's done-when asks that a test "requests its sprint route and asserts the sprint renders", but sprint existence is owned by the Python discovery layer (`reckon/serve.py` `/_discover` / `discover_plans`) and rendered by `docs/ui/sprint.jsx`; the landed pin correctly asserts the owner's output instead.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed. §3's phase change substitutes the live view's single `crew.classify_pointer` classification for the stream-age heuristic inside `_crew_rows`, so every crew surface reads one judgement, not a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — no shared infrastructure is forked: §2 extends the project-state north-star owner and the one scan at `reckon/roadmap.py:2331`, §3 extends `_crew_rows`/`classify_pointer`, §4 extends the discovery owner. Two caveats are carried as findings.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched and extends existing owners: §2 reuses the landed `north_stars` project-state write path (`reckon/project_state.py`, e8efbc7), the `plan-north-star` field (`reckon/_plan_html.py:158`) and the roadmap's existing `undeclared-north-star` / `unoriented-plan` scan (`reckon/roadmap.py:2331`); §3 extends `_crew_rows` (`reckon/serve.py:703`) and `classify_pointer` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:7789`); §4 reuses the `_discover` sprint scan.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no thin layer over existing machinery. §3 keeps one residual stream-age branch inside the existing owner; it is a mechanical fallback, not a parallel path.
